cards.explanation: The offering comes from anyone whose heart moves him to give. God tells Moses, "You are to receive My offering from every man whose heart compels him." (Exodus 25:2) So nobody gets drafted, friends. The gift comes from a heart that wants to give, and I think that's the best kind of gift.
The word is "dwell." God says, "And they are to make a sanctuary for Me, so that I may dwell among them." (Exodus 25:8) Among them, friends, not far off from them. That's a word worth reading twice.

The answer is False. God tells Moses to make the tabernacle and "…design all its furnishings according to the pattern I show you." (Exodus 25:9) So the design isn't Moses' call, friends. I wish my chocolate chip habits worked like that, because I eyeball everything.

The poles are for carrying the ark. God says to insert the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark "…in order to carry it." (Exodus 25:14) Gold rings, gold-covered poles, and a clear job, friends. No guessing needed.

What goes inside the ark is the Testimony God will give Moses. God says, "And place inside the ark the Testimony, which I will give you." (Exodus 25:16) Listen to those words, friends, "…which I will give you." Most of this passage is God telling people what to build, and here He says what He Himself will hand over.

God says He will meet with Moses there. He says, "And I will meet with you there above the mercy seat, between the two cherubim that are over the ark of the Testimony…" (Exodus 25:22) He adds that He will speak with Moses about all He commands regarding the Israelites. God shows up, friends, and He talks.

The answer is True. The table gets rings "…to serve as holders for the poles used to carry the table." (Exodus 25:27) And the poles are acacia wood overlaid with gold, so the table may be carried with them (Exodus 25:28). Same plan as the ark, friends, and it works.
The pitchers and bowls are for pouring drink offerings. They are "…for pouring drink offerings." and they're made of pure gold. (Exodus 25:29) Even the pouring gear gets the gold treatment, friends.

What goes on the table is the Bread of the Presence. God says, "And place the Bread of the Presence on the table before Me at all times." (Exodus 25:30) Look at those two phrases, friends, "before Me" and "…at all times." This bread isn't a one-time thing. It's meant to be there again and again. I know a little about being set in one spot for a long, long time, and I'm glad I got called out of that drawer.

The answer is False. The text never says "only on feast days." God says, "And place the Bread of the Presence on the table before Me at all times." (Exodus 25:30) That's a standing instruction, friends, not an occasional one.

The word is "light." God says, "Make seven lamps and set them up on the lampstand so that they illuminate the area in front of it." (Exodus 25:37) Seven little lamps on one gold stand, all shining on the space in front of it. I spent years in a dark junk drawer, friends, so trust me, a light in the room changes everything.
